INTRODUCTION

=== page 3 ===
NLC India Limited01It’s been nearly seven decades since we have been mining lignite to power the nation. 
Often dubbed ‘brown coal’, lignite is crucial as an abundant, low-cost, and reliable domestic fuel to produce electricity. As the country’s largest lignite miner, we have been serving India through every phase of its development.
Our Navratna status makes us responsive to an evolving market dynamics and keeps 
us responsible for India’s economic progress. Our commitment to the making of a developed India reflects in our resolve to stay in sync with the transition sweeping through the power sector. While keeping the core intact, we are building our renewable capacity steadily, holding firm on the reliability the country depends on.
This steady shift towards renewables makes the theme for this year's annual report. 
The document reflects the dynamism of a company that is stepping up, gaining pace and building strength for the road ahead.
At NLC India, we define resilience as the ability to prepare for tomorrow based on 
today’s performance. We are running our mines and power stations at their best and, at the same time, raising our renewable capacity and opening new lines of growth in energy storage, critical minerals and clean technologies.
This momentum draws on the financial strength that funds our growth, the capability 
and the drive of our people, the research and partnerships that carry us from a resource base to create value for our stakeholders and build their confidence in us. These forces complement one another, keeping us resilient and in step with a rapidly changing landscape.

community well-being. Through innovative practices in resource management, conservation efforts and environmental restoration, NLCIL is creating a positive impact on people and the planet. The Company is paving the way for a greener, more sustainable future while supporting the growth and development of the communities they serve.

70th Integrated Annual Report FY 2025-26 06About the Report
NLC India Limited (NLCIL) is proud to present its fifth Integrated Annual 
Report, setting out a complete account of how the Company has performed across financial and non-financial dimensions during FY 2025-26. Through these pages, we share the milestones reached, the ground covered, initiatives carried forward during the year and as on date providing our stakeholders with the clarity they need to form their own judgements. The report reflects our continuing endeavour to build enduring value and conduct our business responsibly as the energy sector around us continues to evolve.
Forward-looking Statements
Certain passages in this report look ahead rather than back, and may be identified by expressions such as 'may', 'expects', 'could', 'intends', 'aims' and the like. Statements of this kind rest on assumptions and estimates that call for judgement and carry uncertainties we are unable to control. Outcomes may therefore turn out differently, and no assurance can be offered that these expectations will be borne out. The assumptions behind them are ones we believe to be reasonable, though should they prove otherwise, the results may take a different course.Data Management
Every operational site within NLCIL applies a common and clearly defined method to gather, measure, compute and examine its performance data. Holding to a single approach across locations gives our disclosures their accuracy and consistency, and allows management to plan and decide on a dependable footing.Responsibility Statement
Placing accurate and complete information before our stakeholders, covering financial, Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) and operational performance alike, remains an obligation we take seriously. This report has taken shape through wide consultation with business units and departments across the organisation, supported by the guidance of those charged with governance. Responsibility for the integrity, objectivity, transparency and fair presentation of what appears in these pages rests jointly with the Board and the Management.Assurance
The account presented here brings together the financial and non-financial dimensions of the Group's performance. Our financial results, on both a standalone and a consolidated basis, have been examined in detail by M/s. Sundaram & Srinivasan, Chartered Accountants and M/s. PKF Sridhar & Santhanam LLP, Chartered Accountants. Engaging two audit firms lends added assurance to the reliability of the financial information we place on record.
Feedback
Open and transparent engagement with our stakeholders, at every point of contact, continues to be a priority for NLCIL, as does responding to their needs and concerns without delay. Shareholders and investors are welcome to write to the Company Secretary at either the registered office or the corporate office. For matters calling for prompt redressal, they may also approach Integrated Registry Management Services Private Limited, the Registrar and Share Transfer Agent for the Company.SUBSIDIARIES

MESSAGE FROM THE CHAIRMAN  
& MANAGING DIRECTOR
A Year of Record Performance
FY 2025-26 has been one of the 
most successful years in NLCIL's history. Your Company achieved its highest-ever annual coal production of 19.14 million tonnes and highest-ever coal dispatch of 17.69 million tonnes since inception. Total power generation stood at 28.94 Billion Units, while renewable energy generation reached an all-time high of 2.26 Billion Units. These achievements reflect our sustained focus on operational excellence, improved asset utilisation and greater efficiency across our businesses. The Company also added 1 GW of generating capacity during the year, further strengthening its position for future growth.
Consolidated revenue from 
operations crossed ₹17,490 crore and Profit After Tax reached an all-time high of ₹3,769 crore. 
Dear Shareholders,
It gives me immense pleasure to present to you the performance and progress of your Company for FY 2025-26 - a year that marks a significant milestone in the journey of NLC India Limited (NLCIL). It has been a year of strong operational performance, financial resilience, strategic expansion and accelerated progress towards building a diversified, future-ready energy enterprise.
As India advances towards the vision of Viksit Bharat @2047, the 
demand for reliable, affordable and sustainable energy is set to grow significantly. NLCIL is uniquely positioned to contribute to this national endeavour through its integrated strengths in mining, thermal power, renewable energy, emerging energy technologies and strategic resources. Our journey is evolving from that of a lignite mining and power generation company into a diversified energy enterprise with a growing pan-India presence.
The resource is 
the foundation of our business, and resilience is what we are building on top of it: a wider geography, lignite and coal as fuel, solar and wind as energy, and storage for supply.Market capitalisation touched 
₹53,774 crore. We achieved 100% collection efficiency from our power beneficiaries and maintained a consistent record of dividend declarations since 1998-99. Capital expenditure of ₹9,131 crore, the highest ever, demonstrates our determination to accelerate capacity creation and strategic growth.
Strengthening the Mining 
Foundation
Mining remains a key pillar of 
our integrated energy model. Talabira-II & III OCP achieved its highest-ever single-day coal production and dispatch; Mine-II recorded its highest-ever annual lignite dispatch of 13.85 million tonnes; and Pachwara South OCP commenced coal production in March 2026. Significant progress was also made in Machhakata (Revised), New Patrapara South and North Dhadu Western Part coal projects.
Our mining excellence has been 
recognised through Five-Star Ratings from the Ministry of Coal, with NLCIL receiving a cumulative 23 Five-Star Ratings. We are also expanding into critical minerals, including phosphorite

Expanding Reliable Power 
Generation
Thermal power continues to 
play a critical role in ensuring reliable and affordable electricity during India's energy transition. Ghatampur Thermal Power Project recorded its highest-ever annual generation of 4.45 Billion Units. With Unit-II successfully commissioned and the remaining unit achieving commercial operation during the year, the three-unit, 3×660 MW supercritical project has emerged as a major capacity addition to NLCIL's generation portfolio.We will place strong emphasis on improving the availability and reliability of existing thermal generating units, optimising their performance and utilising available capacity to the maximum extent possible. Through condition monitoring, preventive and predictive maintenance, renovation and modernisation, and improved operating practices, we will strive for maximum achievable capacity and efficiency while strengthening reliability and cost competitiveness. Biomass co-firing, carbon capture research and recovery of rare earth elements from fly ash further demonstrate our commitment to reducing the environmental footprint of conventional generation.
Accelerating the Renewable 
Energy Transition
Renewable energy has emerged as 
one of NLCIL's strongest growth engines. During FY 2025-26, we added 352.80 MW of solar capacity—the highest annual addition in the last six years—and achieved our highest-ever single-day renewable energy generation of 9.318 MU. We commissioned the 300 MW Barsingsar Solar Project, a 50 MW solar project at Neyveli and additional rooftop solar capacity.
Our RE Project pipeline 
encompasses large-scale solar, wind-solar hybrid and battery energy storage projects secured from SECI, NTPC, NHPC, GUVNL, NCRTC and other agencies. The 250 MW/500 MWhr BESS project, 600 MW Solar Project with 300 MW/1,800 MWh Battery Energy Storage System and the 4 MW PEM electrolyser-based Green Hydrogen Pilot Plant at Neyveli mark important steps towards firm renewable energy and emerging clean-energy technologies.
Strategic Partnerships, 
Sustainability and People
NLCIL has created partnerships 
with NPCIL, NALCO, IOCL, OREDA and other public sector enterprises, as well as IIT (ISM) Dhanbad, CSIR-CECRI and IIT Madras, opening opportunities in power, renewables, storage, critical minerals, rare earth elements, advanced technologies and Research & Innovation. The Government's approval for additional investment of ₹7,000 crore in NLC India Renewables Limited provides necessary flexibility to accelerate our renewable energy ambitions.Sustainability is integral to our business. Mine reclamation, afforestation, water conservation, biodiversity enhancement, renewable energy development on mined-out land and waste-to-wealth initiatives demonstrate our commitment to responsible resource management. Safety always remains non-negotiable. Technology-enabled reporting, audits, training and enhanced awareness continue to strengthen our safety systems, while Talabira-II & III OCP remains accident-free since inception and Barsingsar Lignite Mine has maintained an accident-free record for six consecutive years.
Our people remain the foundation 
of our transformation. We will continue to promote learning, innovation, merit, accountability and excellence, while strengthening employee welfare and digital capabilities. As our operations become increasingly digital, cybersecurity occupies an important position in organisational resilience.
Creating Value Beyond Business
NLCIL remains committed to inclusive growth and community development.  
Our CSR initiatives cover healthcare, education, skill development, accessibility, rural infrastructure and community well-being. NLCIL General Hospital has benefited approximately 1.20 lakh patients from peripheral villages of Each of these draws

Looking Ahead: From Vision to 
Execution
As NLCIL enters its 70th year, our 
focus is on converting strategic 
vision into timely execution, strengthening operational excellence, maximising utilisation of existing assets and delivering sustainable growth. In thermal power, stabilisation of Ghatampur thermal units and improving availability, reliability and efficiency of existing units will remain priorities. In mining, continuous coal production from Pachwara South OCP, the Talabira-II & III and Kurwa railway sidings, progress on Machhakata (Revised) and New Patrapara South, and securing critical land at Neyveli for mining operations will strengthen fuel security and logistics.
Renewable energy will remain 
a key growth engine, with focus on the commissioning of 600 MW GUVNL Solar Project, 250 MW/500 MWh BESS in Tamil Nadu, 200 MW Solar Project in Gujarat and 150 MW wind-solar hybrid projects, while pursuing further capacity through competitive bidding. We will also expand our critical minerals portfolio and pursue green hydrogen, digitalisation, Artificial Intelligence and strategic partnerships.
Under Corporate Plan 2030 and 
Vision Document 2047, our aspiration is to move towards 20 GW of power generation capacity, beyond 100 MTPA of mining capacity and a significantly larger renewable energy and storage portfolio. Our journey towards Maharatna status by 2030 will be supported by sustained financial performance, disciplined capital allocation, project execution, governance excellence and value creation for all stakeholders.

NLC India at a Glance 
NLC India Limited is a Navratna enterprise under the 
Ministry of Coal, Government of India. For close to seven decades, we have held a place at the centre of India’s energy story. Incorporated in 1956 to develop lignite reserves at Neyveli, we built something the country had not attempted before, which was a fully integrated mining and power complex. From that beginning, we have grown into an integrated energy enterprise, operating across 10 states and one Union Territory, with our corporate office at Neyveli in Tamil Nadu and registered office at Chennai.
Our integrated mine-to-megawatt model remains our 
defining strength. We mine the fuel, we generate the power, and we do both at a scale that keeps our costs contained and our supply secure. Pit head thermal stations sited alongside our own mines allow us to serve base load demand dependably, hour after hour, through seasons. It is a model that has earned the country's confidence and delivered 48 unbroken years of profitability and 26 consecutive years of dividend, a record few enterprises of our vintage can claim.
That same pioneering instinct now carries us into a 
wider portfolio. We were the first Central Public Sector Enterprise in the country to cross a gigawatt of solar capacity, and we are building towards 10,110 MW of renewable capacity by 2030. Alongside this, we have entered battery energy storage, secured two critical mineral blocks in Chhattisgarh, and begun work on a green hydrogen facility at Neyveli. Seven decades on, our purpose stands where it always has, which is to create wealth for well-being.

MINING
Mining is where we began and where our operational 
depth runs deepest. We work six mines across Tamil Nadu, Rajasthan, Odisha and Jharkhand, with a sanctioned capacity of 50.10 MTPA comprising 30.10 MTPA of lignite and 20 MTPA of coal. Our lignite operations at Neyveli and Barsingsar supply our pit head thermal stations directly, while our coal mines at Talabira in Odisha and Pachwara South in Jharkhand serve both captive requirements and external customers.
We are the country's largest lignite producer, accounting for 
close to half of national output. During the year, we produced 19.14 MT of coal from the Talabira II and III OCP and dispatched 17.69 MT, both the highest we have recorded. Pachwara South, with a capacity of 9 MTPA, commenced coal production in March 2026 and adds a new source of long-term fuel security.50.10 MTPA Sanctioned mining capacity

NLCIL is built around three businesses that feed 
one another. We mine lignite and coal, we convert that fuel into power at stations built alongside the mines, and we generate clean energy from the sun and the wind across the country. Around this core sits a growing set of newer businesses, taking us into energy storage, critical minerals and green hydrogen. What binds the portfolio together is its integration: fuel raised from our own mines feeds our own plants, and the earnings from that dependable core fund our move into cleaner sources.Our Business

R ENEWABLE POWER
Our renewable business has grown from an early foothold into 
a business in its own right. We hold 1,785 MW of operational Solar, wind and BESS Capacity spread across Tamil Nadu, Rajasthan, Odisha, Andaman and other states, and we were the first Central Public Sector Enterprise in the country to cross a gigawatt of solar.
NLC India Renewables Limited, our wholly owned subsidiary, 
now anchors this growth. During the year, seven operational renewable projects were transferred to it, and it holds a further 5,810 MW under implementation and 3,885 MW through joint ventures. We commissioned the 300 MW solar plant at Barsingsar, our largest at a single location, and generated 2.26 BU of green power, the most we have produced in a year.1,785 MW Operational renewable capacity

We operate 6,620 MW of installed thermal capacity, of which 3,640 MW sits directly with us and 2,980 MW with our joint venture companies, NLC Tamil Nadu Power Limited and Neyveli Uttar Pradesh Power Limited. Our stations at Neyveli and Barsingsar benefit from a pit-head lignite arrangement, significantly reducing long-distance fuel transportation and the associated emissions. This integrated mine-to-power model ensures reliable fuel supply, improves operational efficiency, reduces fuel logistics and transportation-related carbon footprint, and supports NLCIL’s broader climate action and decarbonisation efforts.
EMERGING BUSINESSES
Beyond generation, we have begun building revenue lines that draw on what we already know and already hold. Our overburden is being converted into manufactured sand through a plant of 1.0 MTPA commissioned at Mine I in February 2026, with commercial sale already under way. We have been declared the successful bidder for the Semhardih and Raipura phosphorite and limestone blocks in Chhattisgarh, carrying 1 MTPA each, and we are working with the Bhabha Atomic Research Centre and Indian Rare Earths Limited on extracting rare earth elements, including from our own fly ash. NLCIL Secured Two critical mineral blocks viz., Parvathapur Block and Govindpur Block in Sangareddy district of Telangana having deposits of Vanadium, Titanium, and Aluminous Laterite.
In energy storage we hold a contracted pipeline of 3,300 MWh 
across three arrangements, of which the 250 MW and 500 MWh project awarded by Tamil Nadu Green Energy Corporation Limited has moved to a signed power purchase agreement. Our green hydrogen plant at Neyveli, drawing on 4 MW of solar, will produce 300 kg of hydrogen a day at a purity of 99.999% over a plant life of 25 years. Five electric vehicle charging stations are being installed across our Neyveli operations.
OUR SUBSIDIARIES AND JOINT VENTURES
We deliver through a group structure that gives each business the focus it needs. NLC India Renewables Limited holds and grows our renewable portfolio and is being prepared for a public listing. NLC India Green Energy Limited manages our diversification businesses. NLC Tamil Nadu Power Limited and Neyveli Uttar Pradesh Power Limited operate our joint venture thermal capacity, and NLC Rajasthan Power Limited carries our lignite-based Thermal Power Project in the state of Rajasthan. Coal Lignite Urja Vikas Private Limited is our joint venture with Coal India Limited. Four step down subsidiaries under NLC India Renewables Limited, namely NIRL Assam Renewables Limited, NIRL Rajasthan Renewables Limited, NIRL NCRTC Renewables Limited and NIRL OREDA Renewables Limited are taking our renewable presence in the State of Assam, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh, respectively.During the year we commenced commercial operation of Unit II of the Ghatampur Thermal Power Project, adding 660 MW and taking Neyveli Uttar Pradesh Power Limited to 1,320 MW. Our thermal stations supplied power to beneficiary states across the country and continued to provide the round the clock reliability that solar and wind cannot yet deliver on their own.

Pan-India Presence

Our Governance Framework
Our governance structure has the Board of Directors at its 
apex, supported by specialised committees and a professional management team. As a Central Public Sector Enterprise with the Government of India controlling 69.47% stake, we are accountable to the as Ministry of Coal, our Shareholders and other stakeholders. We govern in line with the Companies Act, 2013, the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, and the Guidelines on Corporate Governance for Central Public Sector Enterprises issued by the Department of Public Enterprises. 
This layered structure keeps our decision-making transparent, 
distributes responsibility clearly, and allows independent oversight of a business that spans several states and multiple energy verticals.Familiarisation of Independent Directors
We recognise that effective independent oversight rests on a clear understanding of our business. Our structured familiarisation process helps the independent directors align with the Company’s vision and mission, make them aware of our profile and subsidiaries, our mining and power operations, our present capacity across mines and power stations, and our production and financial performance. During the reporting year, familiarisation extended to the priorities shaping our next phase of growth, including our Corporate Plan 2030, our capacity addition programme across thermal and renewable energy, our entry into energy storage and critical minerals, and our research and development initiatives with leading national institutions. The directors are also briefed on their roles, duties and responsibilities, and on the evolving regulatory environment.Risk Management and Internal Controls
We predict, pre-empt, and prevent risks through a structured, Board-supervised framework. The Risk Management Committee at the Board level, supported by various panels under the Board of Directors, identifies, evaluates and monitors the risks facing the Company and charts out the mitigation strategy. The risks can be both external and internal. Our internal control systems, reviewed by the Audit Committee and tested by internal and statutory audit, give the Board the assurance that our assets are safeguarded and our reporting is reliable. As we diversify into new businesses and geographies, this framework helps us take considered risks while protecting the interests of our stakeholders.
Ethics, Integrity and Compliance
Integrity guides how we operate. We run the business under a Code of Conduct that applies to our Board members and the senior management personnel. We maintain strict vigil to ensure transparency and accountability across the organisation. Our procurement and investment decisions follow established, transparent processes, including participation in competitive bidding and public auctions for renewable capacity, coal and critical mineral blocks. We meet our statutory and regulatory obligations by following guidelines laid out by the Companies Act and the SEBI Regulations, and by making timely and accurate disclosures.
We reinforce this through our Integrity Pact programme, 
implemented with the Central Vigilance Commission and Transparency International India, which forms part of our procurement process and applies to every tender above ₹1 crore. The framework extends to our employees, suppliers, contractors, consultants, joint ventures and subsidiaries. During FY 2025-26 we conducted awareness and training programmes on anti-corruption, ethical business conduct and the prevention of anti-competitive practices, ran sessions on regulatory change and compliance requirements, and strengthened our enterprise risk management practices to identify and mitigate governance and compliance risks.
Policies and Disclosures
We have a framework of Board-approved policies that supports consistent and compliant conduct across the Company, including our policies on related-party transactions, material events, document preservation and website disclosure. In keeping with the Regulation 30 of the SEBI Listing Regulations, we disclose material events and other information on our website and retain them for the periods set out in our Archival Policy, so that our stakeholders have access to the information.As a Government Company, the remuneration of our Board-level Directors is fixed by the Government of India as the appointing authority, while the remuneration of our executives and non-unionised supervisors follows the guidelines of the Department of Public Enterprises, and the wages and service conditions of our workmen are governed by settlements with the recognised trade unions. 
The scope of our Nomination and Remuneration Committee 
is limited to matters below Board level, where it considers and recommends performance related pay in line with those guidelines. Our remuneration is therefore not linked directly to environmental, social and governance performance indicators.
As a Government Company we are also exempt, under circulars 
of the Ministry of Corporate Affairs, from the provisions of the Companies Act governing the manner of performance evaluation of the Board, its Committees and individual Directors, and from the corresponding provisions of Schedule IV relating to Independent Directors, where the administrative Ministry specifies the evaluation framework.
Stakeholders and Investors 
We engage our shareholders and the wider investor community with openness and regularity. During the year, we hosted institutional investor interactions, including our Q2 and Q4 FY 2025-26 Institutional Investors Meet at Mumbai, where our leadership presented the Company's performance, strategy and outlook and responded to questions directly. With a shareholder base of more than three lakh, a record of dividends sustained over 26 years and profitability over 48 years, we treat clear, two-way communication as central to the trust we hold.
Governance in a Year of Strategic Change
During the year under review, we took some significant strategic steps, and our governance held firm through each of them. Our Board and the relevant authorities approved the transfer of renewable assets to NLC India Renewables Limited, a wholly Owned Subsidiary and an alternative mechanism for its listing. Cleared the formation of joint ventures for nuclear generation with NPCIL and for renewable capacity with NCRTC, and oversaw capacity additions and new project approvals across the portfolio.Sound governance has anchored the way we create value at NLC India Limited. As a Navratna enterprise, 
we work at the meeting point of public purpose and commercial discipline, with the governance framework built to carry both. In a year when we widened our presence across mining, thermal power, renewables, energy storage, critical minerals and emerging clean energy businesses, that framework gave our diversification the structure, the oversight and the accountability it needed. We celebrated our Raising day on 26th May, 2026, and the confidence placed in us by the Government of India State Government, Regulators, Discoms, JV Partners, Trade Unions, Associations our regulators, and more than 3 lakh shareholders continue to shape how we govern.Governance

Shri Sanoj Kumar Jha is a graduate in physics from Hindu College 
(University of Delhi). He holds M.Sc. degree in public policy and management from King's College, London (UK). He also did his Master's in Advanced Management Programme in Public Policy from the Indian School of Business (ISB). He has done several trainings in the fields of trade, infrastructure, environment, power, economics, data analysis and global poverty.
Shri Sanoj Kumar Jha is a distinguished 1997-batch Indian 
Administrative Service (IAS) officer of the Sikkim cadre. He currently serves the Government of India as the Additional Secretary to the Ministry of Coal. With nearly three decades of administrative experience, he is a seasoned bureaucrat with extensive expertise spanning central, state, and international governance frameworks.
Entrusted with the additional charge of Chairman and Managing

Previously held additional charge as the interim Chairman and 
Managing Director (CMD) of Coal India Limited, India's premier Maharatna public sector undertaking and the world's largest coal producer, driving its critical production targets from November to December 2025. 
As Additional Secretary in the Ministry of Coal, Shri Jha leads 
critical policy implementation, administrative oversight, and structural reforms within India’s solid fuel sector. His deep background in energy and resource management is reflected in top-tier public sector leadership responsibilities

Stakeholder Engagement
At NLC India Limited, our stakeholders form the point of convergence where our business blueprint 
meets the expectations of the nation we serve. Across our mining, thermal and renewable businesses, the relationships we hold with our employees, suppliers, customers, regulators, knowledge institutions, communities and investors are seamlessly blended into the way we plan, operate and grow. We treat sustained dialogue with each of these groups as a structured policy, rather than an occasional exercise, since the insights they offer shape our priorities and guide the allocation of our resources towards the areas of greatest and most lasting impact.
Our approach to engagement responds to the evolving business dynamics of the energy sector and 
to the distinct concerns of every stakeholder group. We engage through defined channels and at a cadence suited to each group, and we carry their feedback into our decision-making at the appropriate levels of the organisation. This continuous exchange strengthens trust, deepens transparency and keeps our strategy aligned with our purpose of creating wealth for the well-being of the nation and of everyone connected with our journey. The framework that follows sets out, for each stakeholder group, why the relationship matters to us, what they expect of us and where we place our priorities, and the manner and frequency of our engagement.
Our employees carry the experience, discipline and 
commitment that run our operations today and equip us for a diversifying energy future.
Expectations and Priorities:• Career advancement, fair appraisal and recognition 
of performance
• Continuous learning and skill enhancement across mining, power and renewables
• A safe, healthy and inclusive workplace
• Physical and mental well-being, welfare and timely communication
How We Engage: We engage our employees through direct communication, in-house publications, structured training programmes, performance appraisal cycles and engagement events, on a monthly, quarterly, annual and need-based footing, with periodic updates placed before the Board.
Our customers, from state utilities drawing power to buyers of lignite, coal and minerals, define the demand that our business exists to serve.
Expectations and Priorities:• Reliable and uninterrupted supply of power
• Consistent quality of lignite, coal and minerals
• Competitive and transparent pricing
• Responsive service and long-term supply security
How We Engage: We engage our customers through 
meetings, conferences, website and email communication, close coordination with distribution utilities under long-term agreements and transparent e-auctions for coal, on a monthly, quarterly and need-based footing.
Recently NLCIL organized a Customers Meet on 25
th 
June 2026 in Chennai, providing an excellent platform for 
interaction with customers. The event facilitated meaningful discussions, addressed customer queries, and helped resolve their concerns effectively.Our suppliers keep our mines, power stations and project sites running, and their reliability underpins the continuity of our operations.
Expectations and Priorities:• Fair, transparent and time-bound procurement practices
• Timely payments and commercial clarity
• Ethical sourcing and sustainability across the supply chain
• Long-term collaboration, capability building and 
business continuity
How We Engage: We engage our suppliers through vendor meets, supplier audits, pre-bid conferences and the Government e-Marketplace, supported by facility visits and vendor development programmes, at events and on a need-based footing.

Importance to Company
Materiality Assessment
Materiality is the lens through which we decide where to focus our attention, our disclosures and our 
resources. Through a structured process, we identify and prioritise the sustainability matters that carry the greatest significance for our business and our stakeholders. The outcome guides our strategy, shapes this report and reflects the issues that influence our operational resilience and our ability to create value for the long-term.
Our list of material topics remains unchanged this year. Alongside the established view of how these 
issues affect our business, we have given clearer weight to how our operations affect the environment, the economy and society, and we have reflected on how the salience of each topic has shifted since last year. This approach keeps us aligned with the GRI Standards, the business responsibility and sustainability report, the capitals of the integrated reporting framework and the sustainable development goals.

of Materiality
This year we read each material topic through 
two complementary dimensions. The first is the significance of the topic to our business, that is, the degree to which it influences our strategy, our financial performance and our resilience. The second is the significance of our own impact, that is, the degree to which our mining, generation and diversification activities affect the environment, the economy and the communities we serve. Reading the two together gives our stakeholders a fuller and more honest account of where our responsibilities and our priorities lie, and it prepares the ground for the more detailed impact disclosures that our sector will increasingly be expected to make.Identification of  
Material Topics
We evaluate our key material 
issues against industry trends, business goals, competitor analysis, global concerns, regulatory policies and stakeholder inputs, categorising them across Environmental, Social and Governance aspects in line with GRI standards.
Alignment with  
Core Strategy
We refine the prioritised 
topics to align them with our strategic objectives and risk management framework, integrating them closely with our business strategy and our long-term goals.Prioritisation
We assess the identified issues for their risks, opportunities and financial implications through extensive consultation with internal and external stakeholders, including employees, suppliers, customers, investors and NGOs, to prioritise the matters of greatest significance.
Validation
The material issues undergo review and validation by our Senior Management Team, including all Functional Directors and the Chairman and Managing Director, so that they are integrated into our decision making.Step 1

Risk Management
The scale and complexity of our operations expose us to a wide spectrum of risks, ranging from 
geological and environmental uncertainties in mining to volatility in the energy market and the regulatory shifts such as the transition to clean energy. We are aware that the manner in which we predict and pre-empt these risks determines the confidence our stakeholders place in the sustainability of our growth.
Risk management is woven into the way we frame our strategy. By embedding governance 
mechanisms, disciplined controls and continuous oversight, we identify, evaluate and mitigate risks early, while remaining alert to the opportunities that a changing energy landscape brings. Our approach aligns the exposures we track with the priorities set out in our materiality assessment, so that the risks we manage and the topics we consider most material move together.
Strategic Risk 
Governance
Our governance framework for 
risk management is aligned with internationally recognised standards, including the COSO Integrated Framework and the ISO 31000:2018 guidelines. This ensures that our practices reflect global best practice while remaining sensitive to the distinct realities of the mining and energy sectors. Oversight is exercised through the Risk Management Committee of the Board, which sets strategic direction and ensures that risk deliberations are integrated into decision-making at the highest levels of the organisation.
We classify our risks under three 
broad categories: Strategic, Business, and Operational. This allows us to differentiate between long-term structural risks, such as energy transition imperatives and regulatory shifts, and operational risks that carry the potential to disrupt day-to-day mining, plant operations or supply chain continuity. Once identified, each risk is assessed through both qualitative and quantitative lenses. This dual-layered analysis empowers us to focus on the risks with the greatest potential impact and likelihood of occurrence, capturing their trend as well as their current position.

Operational Control, Compliance and Assurance
We have institutionalised rigorous internal controls across contracts, procurement, project execution and human resources. Authorised manuals and process frameworks govern each of these domains, ensuring consistency, compliance and accountability, and maintaining clarity of procedure in the day-to-day functioning of our business.
We stress on transparency and independent assurance. Leading 
Chartered Accountant firms conduct comprehensive audits across our mines, thermal stations and renewable energy sites. These reviews validate the reliability of our financial and operational systems alongside our internal controls. Audit outcomes are subject to rigorous scrutiny by the Audit Committee, in close consultation with internal and statutory auditors so that any emerging risk is addressed promptly and decisively.
We reinforce this discipline with a proactive risk culture. Our 
employees undergo regular trainings on the challenges of mining, power generation and renewable project execution. Quarterly risk evaluations are carried out by the Internal Risk Review Committee, with subsequent reviews by the Board-level Risk Management Committee and the Audit Committee, keeping us agile in responding to shifting market conditions, environmental obligations and technological developments.Risk Profile

RISK MANAGEMENT
Risk Prioritisation and Response
We prioritise our risks so that our resources and oversight are directed where they are most needed. Risks with higher probability and 
severity are elevated for closer scrutiny, while those with reduced impact are monitored with proportionate intensity. Our approach distinguishes between four states.
Our Risk Landscape
We treat risk mitigation as a strategic enabler of sustainable growth. Across our strategic, operational and business risks, we combine rigorous planning, technological innovation and proactive engagement with stakeholders to safeguard the continuity of our operations while capturing opportunities in India's evolving energy landscape. Link to Material Topics 
Resource Availability, Land Acquisition 
Capital Most AffectedResidual Direction
Stable Exposure: Access to land underpins the continuity of our mining operations, and delays in acquisition can interrupt lignite and coal availability. Diverse ownership patterns, state-specific legal frameworks and local sensitivities can extend project timelines and raise costs, and land constraints at certain mines have drawn auditor attention. 
Controls and Response: We pursue land access through a multi-state 
approach aligned with the RFCTLARR Act, 2013 and the CBA Act, 1957, supported by fair and transparent rehabilitation and resettlement, digital land-management tools and grievance redressal. Sustained engagement with district administrations, communities and regulators has restored land and secured continuity at our key mines.
RENEWABLE TARIFFS AND REGULATORY DELAYS 
Link to Material Topics 
Renewable energy 
Capital Most AffectedResidual Direction
Stable Exposure: Preferential tariff schemes and commissioning deadlines set by regulators shape the returns on our renewable portfolio. Missed deadlines risk the forfeiture of tariff benefits, and unrecovered dues can affect project economics. 
Controls and Response: We manage delivery through advance planning of 
land and connectivity, and we maintain close engagement with regulators on tariff and commissioning matters. Our competitive-bidding discipline and improving plant performance protect margins across the portfolio.
ENERGY TRANSITION AND DIVERSIFICATION EXECUTION
Link to Material Topics 
Climate strategy, renewable energy 
Capital Most AffectedResidual Direction
Rising Exposure:  Our shift towards a balanced portfolio, spanning 
renewables, storage, nuclear and critical minerals, carries execution and capital allocation risk. New verticals such as our proposed nuclear joint venture with NPCIL and our entry into critical minerals sit outside our traditional lignite and thermal expertise, and mis-sequencing investment or capability could strain returns. 
Controls and Response: We enter each new vertical through a disciplined 
evaluation of returns and national need, and through joint ventures and institutional partnerships that bring proven capability. We phase our capital commitments against project maturity, and we retain our regulated thermal and mining base as a stable foundation while the new businesses scale.

Link to Material Topics 
Operational efficiency and plant reliability   
Capital Most AffectedResidual Direction
Reducing Exposure:  The sustained operation of certain assets, 
notably the Circulating Fluidised Bed Combustion boilers at the TPS-II Expansion, has historically led to generation inefficiencies and fixed-cost under-recovery. 
Controls and Response: We completely revamped the boiler of one unit 
with OEM support and independent expert review, lifting its availability past 90% and materially improving generation. Modification of the remaining unit is in progress, supported by continuous monitoring and proactive intervention.

Link to Material Topics 
Operational efficiency and plant reliability   
Capital Most AffectedResidual Direction
Stable Exposure: Variability in power demand and the surrender of contracted power by customers can threaten revenue stability and asset utilisation, as seen when units are placed under reserve shutdown during periods of low demand. 
Controls and Response: We optimise surrendered power through 
participation in power exchanges and bilateral contracts, which cushions the revenue impact and preserves flexibility in a dynamic market. Our fleet responds to grid demand across the cycle, with most units maintaining high availability during peak periods.
ENERGY STORAGE AND GRID INTEGRATION 
Link to Material Topics 
Renewable energy, operational efficiency and plant reliability  
Capital Most AffectedResidual Direction
Rising Exposure:  The reliability of our renewable expansion depends 
on the timely delivery of battery and pumped storage and on grid connectivity. Delays in storage commissioning or transmission availability could strand renewable capacity or leave us with tight completion windows, since our storage awards carry an 18-month delivery obligation. 
Controls and Response: We apply for connectivity in advance of 
project completion, and we internally target delivery well inside the permitted window. We are building storage across technologies, both battery and pumped, and we sequence storage alongside generation so that renewable output can be integrated reliably into the grid.

Sustainability Policy Framework
Our Sustainability Policy is the umbrella under which we set out how we grow responsibly across our 
mining, power and renewable operations. It brings together our overarching ESG commitments and a set of specific policies that put those commitments into practice.
The framework is designed with three levels. A set of enabling policies translates those principles into 
action on defined operational matters. Both connect to the topics we have identified as material and to the risks we manage, so that our intent, our priorities and our safeguards stay aligned.
Level One: Our ESG Policy
Our ESG Policy ambit covers all our establishments, including subsidiaries and joint ventures, and rests on balancing economic, 
environmental and social responsibility.Level Two: Enabling Policies
These policies give effect to our ESG principles on specific operational matters.
Level Three: Alignment and Review
Read together, our Sustainability Policy, our ESG principles and our enabling policies describe one commitment from three angles: what we stand for, where it matters most, and how we protect it. We review our ESG Policy at least once every three years, and sooner if the need arises, so that the framework keeps pace with our business and the expectations of our stakeholders.
ENVIRONMENTAL 
We commit to integrated management systems with continual improvement, climate change mitigation and adaptation, biodiversity management through bio-reclamation, sustainable water management, the 6R approach to waste, and lowering our carbon footprint through carbon capture and green technologies.

Our strong cash generation, healthy net worth and access to concessional green finance give us the room to fund our diversification, to hold a stable base of regulated returns, and to pursue our growth ambitions while keeping our balance sheet resilient.

Credit Rating Outlook

Manufactured 
Capital
Manufactured Capital is the physical backbone of our integrated energy business, spanning our 
opencast mines, our thermal stations and our growing fleet of solar, wind and storage assets. Our focus on modern infrastructure and advanced extraction and generation technology has strengthened operational efficiency while easing our environmental footprint. By integrating mining with power generation, much of it at pit head, we sustain a reliable fuel-to-power chain that underpins the continuity of energy supply to the nation.
Linkage to Corporate Plan 2030
Our present assets build towards our 2030 targets of mining 
capacity of around 104 MTPA, thermal capacity above 10 GW and renewable capacity above 10 GW, moving us towards a balanced fifty-fifty thermal and renewable mix.
Material Issues
• Land acquisition
• Resource availabilityCreating Value from What We Produce 
We turn resources, expertise and investment into the physical foundations of our energy business – from installed capacity and reliable generation to the infrastructure that enables us to diversify and grow. The outputs are the power we supply to the nation and the fuel we produce for our own stations and for sale, and the outcomes are energy security, the steady growth of our renewable base, and the modernisation of assets that have served for decades. In doing so, we manage real trade-offs, balancing thermal dependability against the transition to cleaner generation, and matching our output to grid demand across the cycle.
A Year of Capacity Milestones
FY26 and as on date we added materially to our installed base. Ghatampur Unit-2 and Unit 3 commenced commercial operation on 9 December 2025 and 13 June 2026, adding 1320 MW to our group capacity and taking it from 5,300 MW to 6620 MW, and lifting our coal-based capacity from 1,660 MW to 2,980 MW. Further, we brought over 1 GW of new capacity into the group during the year, comprising 660 MW of thermal and 352.80 MW of renewables, and we commenced coal production at our Pachwara South block. Our coal production at Talabira reached an all-time high of 19.14 million tonnes, and our renewable power generation reached an all-time high of 2.26 billion units — evidence of an asset base that is both expanding and diversifying.
Thermal Power Generation
Our thermal stations remain the dependable core of our generation and, during FY 2025-26, we ran them with an emphasis on the availability and readiness to meet grid demand. Overall generation across several stations reflected a period of subdued demand during the year, when a number of units were placed under reserve shutdown in line with grid requirements, before demand recovered later in the period. Our focus through this cycle was on keeping our units available and reliable, so that we could respond whenever the grid called on us.

We continued to modernise our thermal fleet in FY 2025-26 to 
enhance reliability and efficiency. At TPS-II Expansion Unit-1, we carried out modification of the Fluidised Bed Heat Exchanger and fixed a modified vortex finder. At NLC Tamil Nadu Power Limited (NTPL), we completed modification of the distributed control system in both the units. And at TPS-II, we introduced an external lube oil system in the mill double bearing to prevent bearing damage caused by lignite puffing. These interventions strengthen the dependability of our stations and support the improved availability we recorded at the modernised units.Automation in Our Mines
Technology and mechanisation determine how safely and how productively we mine. We practise blast-free mining across all our operations: bucket wheel excavators with belt conveyors and spreaders at Neyveli, conventional equipment at Barsingsar for both overburden and lignite, and surface miners for coal at Talabira. Every item of heavy earth-moving machinery carries an automatic fire detection and suppression system, and during the year we extended the same protection to 18 blast-hole drilling machines, six each at Mine-I, Mine-IA and Mine-II.
Our bucket wheel excavators ran well through the year. 
We completed major revamping of three machines, two of them ahead of schedule, and we brought down maintenance turnaround sharply. At Mine-IA we upgraded the conveyor system to higher-capacity 2,000 mm belts, and conveyor reliability improved across our Neyveli mines through fewer joints and fewer joint failures.
Digitalisation ran through much of this work. We commissioned 
an RFID-based digital lock-out and tag-out system at Mine-II, with extension planned to Mine-I and Mine-IA, and installed audio-visual alarm systems with LED alerts and public announcements on the Mine-II conveyors. We implemented GPS-based tracking for our vehicles in the Neyveli mines, together with a fuel management system built on RFID dispensing, GPS monitoring and anti-theft control. At Talabira, a digital logistics management system now operates at two weighbridges, giving us real-time visibility of coal despatch. We took up an integrated command and control centre for our mines, alongside variable frequency drives, dynamic loading systems, belt weighing systems, magnetic separators and real-time conveyor monitoring. Three-dimensional mine models, animated standard operating procedures and digital safety displays strengthened how we train our people, and terrestrial laser scanning with DGPS surveys improved our mine surveying across Neyveli and beyond. We also ordered four 160 mm diesel crawler-mounted blast-hole drills for Mine-IA and Mine-II, built to DGMS safety requirements.
Dust suppression across our mines is supported by 30 water 
sprinklers and six fog cannons, with four road-sweeping machines and five motor graders maintaining our haul roads, and continuous monitoring of respirable dust and ambient air quality.

MANUFACTURED CAPITAL
Reducing Environmental Impact of 
Thermal Power
We are progressively lowering the environmental impact of our 
thermal generation while continuing to supply reliable electricity. We are doing so through the adoption of high-efficiency power generation technologies, biomass co-firing, and advanced emission control systems, and through our carbon capture research with IIT Madras. We practise scientific fly ash management and the recovery of critical minerals from ash, integrate renewable energy, conserve water, and apply digital optimisation and robust environmental management systems across our operations. Together, these measures support India's transition towards cleaner and more sustainable energy, and they connect this capital directly to the research described in our Intellectual Capital and the stewardship discussed in our Natural Capital.Mining and Production
Our mining operations supply the fuel that underpins our thermal generation, and FY 2025-26 was a year of contrast across our two fuels. Our coal production at Talabira reached an all-time high of 19.14 million tonnes, up from 17.20 million tonnes, and coal despatch from the same project reached 17.69 million tonnes, also the highest since the project began. We commenced production at our Pachwara South coal block during the year, strengthening the fuel security of our power portfolio and adding good-quality coal for sale in the open market over and above our own requirement. Our lignite production stood at 21.27 million tonnes in line with the fuel demands of the linked end use plants, lower than the 24.06 million tonnes of the previous year, reflecting a planned shift in output across our Neyveli mines as our fuel mix changes. Overburden removal at Mine-II reached 94.38 million cubic metres, the highest the mine has recorded.The year also brought recognition for how we mine and new ways of selling what we produce. The Ministry of Coal has now conferred 23 Five-Star Ratings on our coal and lignite operations, and for FY 2023-24 it rated Mine-IA, Talabira II and III and Barsingsar at five stars and Mine-I and Mine-II at four. We migrated the e-auction of lignite, coal, minor minerals and overburden from an outsourced platform to our own NeAT portal, and we introduced special long-term auctions with a validity of 360 days to give our customers greater certainty of supply. We became the first in India to commercialise the sale of overburden, from Mine-IA, and of washed silica sand, from Mine-I. The Government of Tamil Nadu has approved the disposal of overburden soil from our external dumps and its conversion into manufactured sand for a period of ten years, extending the circular-economy work described in our Natural Capital.
Renewable Energy Capacity
Our renewable portfolio is the fastest-growing part of our asset base, and it is central to the diversification of our Manufactured Capital. During FY 2025-26, our renewable energy generation reached an all-time high of 2.26 billion units, and we added 352.80 MW of renewable capacity to the group. Our operational renewable capacity stood at 1,785 MW as on date with a substantial portfolio under implementation, positioning renewables as a defining element of our future generation mix.
Building Towards 2030
We have framed our asset strategy with the idea of reaching a balanced and resilient portfolio by 2030. We are working towards a mining capacity of around 104 million tonnes per annum, and more than 10GW each of thermal and renewable capacities that would drive us towards a balanced mix of electricity. In this way, the infrastructure we build today, from our modernised thermal stations to our expanding renewables fleet, turns our resource base into lasting resilience, and carries the strength of our past into the energy system of the future.

Intellectual 
Capital
Intellectual Capital is the applied knowledge, research and technology through which we draw more 
from every tonne we mine. Our research centre and our partnerships with premier institutions let us recover materials of national importance from lignite and fly ash, advance clean energy technology, and build the capability our diversification demands. Alongside, our digitisation of mining and enterprise systems sharpens our efficiency and the quality of our decisions, keeping us competitive.
Our research is strategic to both our operational targets and 
our sustainability objectives. Through our cross-functional collaborations, we address immediate technical challenges while supporting the transition to more efficient and cleaner operations. We focus on projects that improve the life of mining equipment, advance the diversification of lignite-based products, and develop renewable energy systems. These initiatives align with priorities such as the National Green Hydrogen Mission. By integrating innovative solutions into our operations, we ensure that our R&D efforts drive progress towards a more sustainable future.

Our R&D Policy
Our R&D policy provides the framework within which our research is pursued. It spans analytical services for quality control of products and materials, the conduct of science and technology research projects, a focus on lignite utilisation, diversification and product development, environmental monitoring, pollution measurement, quality control testing and consultancy, and technology development, patenting and commercialisation. Research proposals are evaluated for innovation, technical feasibility, scalability, economic viability and alignment with our business before they are approved, so that our research stays disciplined and focused on outcomes.Key Focus Areas of Our R&D
Our research efforts are woven around a set of focus areas that connect directly to our business. We pursue R&D to boost production in mining and power generation through innovative solutions and data. We develop energy-efficient, eco-friendly technologies for our mining and thermal plants to conserve resources. We foster grassroot-level R&D initiatives within our production units to deliver both short-term and long-term gains. We undertake research on environmental sustainability and fuel security to combat climate change. We strengthen our R&D capabilities at CARD to meet international standards in collaboration with global and local institutions. And we pursue patents and commercialisation opportunities from our R&D outcomes to enhance NLCIL's reputation and professional development.Centre for Applied Research and Development (CARD)
The Centre for Applied Research and Development has become the cornerstone of our innovation. Established in 1958 as the Central Laboratory and renamed CARD in 1975, it was recognised by the Department of Scientific and Industrial Research and has since been at the forefront of driving technological advancement and operational efficiency within the Company. 
CARD's mission is to focus on research and development that aligns with our strategic goals of sustainability, operational excellence 
and technological leadership.

INTELLECTUAL CAPITAL
Driving Innovation and 
Sustainability
We recognise the crucial role that innovation and sustainability 
play in shaping the future of the energy sector. With efforts to allocate capital for developing clean energy solutions, we are contributing to a sustainable future. In FY 2025-26, we advanced the initiatives we set out to pursue.
Renewable Energy Investment
We continue to make substantial investment in expanding our renewable energy capacity, including solar and wind projects, which contribute to diversifying our energy portfolio and achieving our carbon reduction targets. This work is carried forward in detail in our Natural and Manufactured Capital.
Green Hydrogen Initiatives
Our exploration of green hydrogen has moved from intent to execution. Our 4 MW green hydrogen pilot at Neyveli, based on Proton Exchange Membrane electrolyser technology, will produce hydrogen by water electrolysis using renewable power, demonstrating a carbon-free production pathway in line with the National Green Hydrogen Mission. We awarded the engineering, procurement and construction contract to M/s InSolare Energy Limited on 3 November 2025, engaged a project management consultant, and commenced site preparation works. We are extending this work into alternative pathways, including biohydrogen from biomass, pursued with Alagappa University, and renewable hydrogen from biogas through solar-driven methane cracking, pursued with Annamalai University.
Exploring Collaborative Innovation
We collaborate with industry leaders, academic institutions and government bodies for advanced research and to implement technologies that support our vision of a sustainable, low-carbon economy. Our partnerships span premier institutions across the country, and they underpin much of the progress reported in this chapter.Creating Value from Lignite and 
Fly Ash
A defining strand of our research is the conversion of our own 
resources and byproducts into materials of national importance. FY 2025-26 saw meaningful progress in this segment.
Activated carbon from lignite and humic acid sludge
We wanted to convert lignite and humic acid sludge, a high-demand material used for water and air purification, into activated carbon. By repurposing carbon-rich sludge from lignite processing, the initiative helps reduce waste and produce activated carbon, contributing to more efficient pollution control while advancing resource conservation and environmental sustainability.
Eco-friendly Geopolymer Bricks
The geopolymer bricks made of fly ash and overburden sand offer a sustainable alternative to conventional building material. Cured using solar heating, instead of traditional kiln firing, these bricks significantly reduce energy consumption and carbon emissions, lowering the carbon footprint of the construction industry. This innovation advanced to a filed patent in April 2025.
Rare Earth Elements from Fly Ash
Our work to extract strategically important rare earth elements from lignite fly ash has progressed from agreement to implementation. An MoU was signed with BARC in August 2025, under which BARC is providing technical support for demonstrating the extraction of REE from fly ash. Studies have confirmed the presence of appreciable quantities of these elements in our fly ash, and the project is progressing towards pilot scale implementation., At present the tender for the pilot plant is in progress. This positions us to contribute to national self-reliance in critical materials from a byproduct of our own operations.
High-purity Silica from Overburden Sand
We are pursuing the beneficiation of overburden silica sand into high-purity silica suitable for solar glass and wafer manufacturing, in collaboration with CSIR-IMMT, turning a mining byproduct into a feedstock for the renewable industry.Innovation Incubation  
Centre at CARD
Our Innovation Incubation Centre, set up at CARD in 
collaboration with IISc Bengaluru and Anna University, focuses on projects across energy, environment and healthcare. Its initiatives include smart IoT-based aeroponic herbal cultivation, membrane-less chemical-free wastewater treatment, hydroponics in backfilled mine areas, and the development of geopolymer green bricks using solar heating. Several of these projects have progressed from the proof of concept to prototype stages during FY 2025-26, reinforcing NLCIL's role as an innovator in energy and environmental sectors.Innovation in Mining and 
Power Generation
Much of our research is directed at the practical challenges of 
running our mines and power stations more safely and efficiently. Our project to prevent premature failures and enhance the life of bottom rollers used in bucket wheel excavators was executed jointly with NIT Trichy and IISc Bengaluru, with financial assistance from the Ministry of Coal (Science and Technology). 
Through a separate collaboration with IISc Bengaluru, we are 
developing indigenous alternatives to expensive tungsten carbide excavator bucket teeth for the mining industry. 
With IIT Hyderabad, we are enhancing boiler inspection in our 
coal and lignite power plants using AI-guided drones equipped with machine learning and thermal imaging capabilities. 
With Annamalai University, Chidambaram, we are building an 
automated monitoring and defect detection system for conveyor belts to improve reliability in mining operations. 
IIITDM Kancheepuram is supporting us in developing an AI 
and vision integrated autonomous mobile system for lignite dust collection. And with NIT Rourkela, we are designing UV-assisted self-cleaning ceramic membrane filters to recycle circulating-water blowdown from our thermal power stations.
We are also working on the materials our own equipment 
depends on and on new routes to energy conversion. With NIT Tiruchirappalli we are developing a new material for bucket wheel excavator teeth to improve wear resistance and service life. Our bottom-roller project with NIT Tiruchirappalli and IISc Bengaluru has passed field evaluation: the newly developed alloys, installed on a Mine-II excavator, showed better resistance to abrasion, wear and corrosion and a longer service life than the rollers they replaced. With Annamalai University we are developing metal-supported solid oxide fuel cells from materials derived from lignite fly ash using atmospheric plasma spray, and with Tamil Nadu Agricultural University we are studying microbial technologies for crop cultivation under our agri-voltaic systems.
Value Addition beyond the Core
Our humic-acid research illustrates how far we can extend value from lignite. With IIT Madras, under a joint development agreement signed in October 2025, we are studying lignite-derived humic acid for semiconductor and optoelectronic applications, working to tailor its optical properties for light-emitting devices and to secure patentable innovations. In parallel, we are evaluating humic acid as a feed additive in brackish-water aquaculture with Annamalai University and as a bio-stimulant for important crops with Tamil Nadu Agricultural University, where field trials are under way across multiple locations.Key Collaborations with NLCIL
We have fostered significant collaborations with leading institutions to strengthen our R&D, and FY 2025-26 saw these partnerships deepen and deliver.
Key partnerships and their progress in FY 2025-26 
• NIT Trichy and IISc Bengaluru: A joint project, with the Ministry of Coal (Science and Technology) support, to prevent premature failures and enhance the life of bottom rollers in bucket wheel excavators. 
• IISc Bengaluru:  Developing indigenous alternatives to 
tungsten carbide excavator bucket teeth, and a partner in our Innovation Incubation Centre. 
• IIT Madras:  exploring semiconductor applications using 
lignite-derived humic acid, advanced to a signed joint development agreement in October 2025. 
• BARC:  A pioneering project to extract rare earth elements 
from fly ash, moved from MoU stage to floating of tender for establishment of pilot-plant.
• CSIR-IMMT:  Beneficiation of overburden sand into 
high-purity silica for the solar industry.

Developing Leaders for Tomorrow 
We build our leadership pipeline through a structured,

Our Board-level executives are nominated through the Department of Public Enterprises for capacity-building and customised leadership programmes at eminent institutions. Our senior executives in the E8 and E9 grades are groomed for future Board-level roles through DAKSH, the government's flagship Common Leadership Development Programme under Mission Karmayogi, and through a five-day capacity development programme at IIM Calcutta under a three-year memorandum of understanding. 
Our E7 grade executives are developed through a five-day 
programme at IIM Nagpur under a similar three-year arrangement, covering project management, risk analysis and financial management, supported by expert-led sessions at our own Centre. In FY 2025-26, 48 executives were trained at IIM Calcutta and 139 at IIM Nagpur.

We believe in growing our people from within, and our career growth policy gives our executives a transparent path of progression built on merit, performance, experience and suitability against available vacancies. At NLCIL, we are deeply committed towards supporting our employees throughout their careers and even after retirement. Welfare of Our Contract Workforce
Our contract workforce works alongside our regular employees across our mines, stations and project sites, and we extend our welfare commitments to them with the same seriousness. During FY 2025-26, we paid a one-time ex-gratia of ₹5,000 to ₹6,000 per worker, over and above the statutory bonus, at a cost of ₹9.78 crore, benefitting around 17,505 contract workmen. We provide free outpatient and inpatient treatment at our Neyveli Hospital to contract workmen engaged in annual maintenance works, along with their dependents.
We support the education of their children through an 
educational assistance scheme for wards pursuing studies beyond school, which has reached 2,528 students over the past five years at an outlay of ₹2.37 crore, and through tuition-fee reimbursement for wards from Scheduled Caste, Scheduled Tribe and Other Backward Class families studying at Jawahar Science College, Neyveli. We provide two sets of stitched uniforms each year to contract workmen in maintenance works, at an annual cost of ₹1.70 crore.
We stand by their families in the hardest moments. Through our 
Contract Workmen Death Relief Fund, we provide a solatium of up to ₹30 lakh in the event of a fatal industrial accident, inclusive of statutory compensation, and up to ₹15 lakh in the event of death during employment for other reasons. Under our Family Relief Scheme, we pay a monthly relief of ₹18,100 to the spouse of a deceased contract workman until the age of 60, with provision for the eldest ward where the spouse has predeceased.
Beyond these, we extend free education to the wards of contract 
workmen at our NLC schools up to Class XII, along with free breakfast, noon meals and uniforms for children in Classes XI and XII, and free school transport within the township. Through the NLC Indcoserve and Howsicos cooperative societies, 2,043 quarters have been allotted to member contract workmen at nominal rent, with water and electricity at subsidised rates.

Health and Safety
Safety as a Foremost Priority
Safety is inseparable from how we mine lignite and generate power. Across our mines, coal operations and thermal stations,  we protect our people through engineered controls, disciplined systems and a culture of shared responsibility. In FY 2025-26, that commitment reflected in our safety performance.

The reduction in our Lost Time Injury Frequency Rate for both our employees and our contract workmen, demonstrated the 
efficacy of our safety systems and our sustained attention to frontline practices. We record these figures for our regular and contract workforce alike.Safety Performance in FY 2025-26Safety in Our Mines
Our mining safety rests on prevention built into the operation itself. We practise blast-free lignite mining across our Neyveli mines using bucket wheel excavators with belt conveyors and spreaders, and blast-free methods at Barsingsar and, for coal extraction, at Talabira through surface miners. Every item of heavy earth-moving machinery is fitted with an Automatic Fire Detection and Suppression System. We have prepared Safety Management Plans for all six mines under the Coal Mines Regulations 2017, based on hazard identification and risk assessment, and we review them every six months. 
To suppress dust, we deploy 30 water sprinklers and six fog 
cannons across our mines, supported by road-sweeping machines and motor graders for haul-road maintenance, and we monitor respirable dust and ambient air quality continuously.
Discipline at the mine gate matters as much as engineering. 
No one enters a mine, whether our own employee or a contractor's, without an initial medical examination, basic vocational training at our Group Vocational Training Centre under the Mines Vocational Training Rules 1966, and a valid entry pass, which CISF personnel check at the single entrance every working shift. We have framed separate standard operating procedures for women employed in the mines. We have conducted scientific studies of slope stability in all our mines under the Coal Mines Regulations 2017 and implemented the recommendations, prepared crisis management plans for every mine, carry out noise surveys in line with DGMS guidance, maintain illumination at the prescribed levels, and have banned mobile phones in working areas in favour of walkie-talkies. On our conveyors, pre-start sirens and public address announcements in the local language, audio-visual blinkers along the belt and lock-out indicator lamps warn our people before machinery moves.Safety in Our Thermal Stations
We ensure safety in our thermal power stations through disciplined operating practices. We enforce strict use of personal protective equipment, carry out routine inspections with immediate corrective action, and conduct toolbox talks before work begins. We have prepared and implemented 600 standard operating procedures for operation and maintenance works, and our stations are subject to external safety audit by the National Safety Council every two years, with observations acted upon in full.
Assurance, Technology and Medical Care
We assure our safety through regular audit and continuous improvements. Our mines undergo internal safety audit by Corporate Safety every year, and Safety and Health Management System audits are conducted and uploaded to the National Coal Mines Safety Report portal in line with Ministry of Coal guidelines. Our NLCIL Aran mobile safety app allows our people to report unsafe observations and near misses for prompt compliance, extending safety awareness to the frontline. Our medical care underpins all of this: initial and periodical medical examinations for everyone engaged in the mines, free cardiac screening for all employees, medical officers trained in ILO chest x-ray classification to detect dust-related illness early, and a first-aid station with an ambulance at every mine and thermal station.
Our Industrial Medical Centre is approved by the Directorate 
General of Mines Safety as a training centre for first aid and issues first-aid competency certificates, and we have imparted this training to everyone working at NLCIL.

Social and 
Relationship Capital
Social and Relationship Capital is the trust we hold with the communities around our operations, 
with our partners and with the wider society we serve. The regions built around our mines and plants share our land and our future, and their well-being sits at the heart of our licence to operate. Through our CSR programmes, our supplier relationships and our sustained community dialogue, we work to create shared value and to keep our growth rooted in the prosperity of the people around us.Our Customers
Our customers include the state distribution utilities that 
draw electricity from our stations, to the buyers who purchase coal from our mines, and each relationship rests on the same footing: reliable supply, consistent quality, and transparent and fair dealings.
Most of our generation reaches the nation through long-term 
power purchase agreements with state distribution utilities. These agreements ensure supply security and stabilises revenue, and we honour them by keeping our units available to meet grid demand across the cycle. The strength of these relationships showed in our numbers this year, with the collection efficiency of our power debtors standing at full recovery. For our coal customers, we operate a transparent e-auction process that gives open access to the good-quality coal produced at Talabira, beyond the quantity we commit to our own stations, extending the value of our resource base into the wider market.
Our Suppliers and Vendors
Our suppliers and vendors keep our mines, stations and project sites running, and their dependability is inseparable from our own. We hold these relationships to a standard of fairness and transparency, and we work to ensure that the economic weight of our operations settles in the regions around us rather than passing them by.
Building Stronger Communities
Beyond our commercial relationships lies our deepest social commitment, the development of the communities living in the vicinity of our mines and plants. Our investment strategy for community development is guided by our Corporate Social Responsibility policy and overseen by the Corporate Social Responsibility Committee of the Board. It is delivered in line with the guidelines of the Ministry of Coal, the Ministry of Corporate Affairs, and the Department of Public Enterprises.
Our approach is participatory and convergence-based. 
We identify needs in direct consultation with the district collectorate, government departments, gram panchayats and local communities, so that what we build answers a genuine local priority. We then deliver through partnership, drawing on district administrations, line departments, educational institutions and competent implementation agencies, and we monitor delivery through Panchayati Raj institutions, Village Development Committees and School Management Committees. This model of shared identification, shared delivery and shared oversight strengthens public institutions, builds community ownership, and creates assets that endure well beyond the year of spending.This principle was visible in how we delivered our community work during the year. A large share of it, from classrooms and school infrastructure to drinking water systems, the rejuvenation of water bodies and sanitation assets, was executed through district rural development agencies, local contractors and district-based implementing authorities, so that project spending circulated within the local economy. We drew on regional construction firms, engineering agencies, equipment suppliers and local service providers to deliver these works, generating employment, building the capacity of local enterprise and improving the reach of services in mining-affected and peripheral areas. A supply chain rooted in the local economy is, for us, both good business and a form of community investment.
Community works delivered through DRDAs, local contractors and district agencies, regional firms, engineering agencies and local suppliers engaged across projects procurement directed to circulate value within our operating regions.
