C) Market risk
  Market risk is the risk that changes in market prices, such as foreign exchange rates, interest rates and equity prices, will affect the 
Group’s income or the value of its holdings of financial instruments. The objective of market risk management is to manage and control market risk exposures within acceptable parameters while optimising returns.D) Currency risk
  The Group enters into import agreements for the purchase of capital goods. Up to March 31, 2016, the Group capitalised exchange gains/losses arising on reinstatement/actual payment of vendor liabilities up to the date of commercial operation. Such capital costs pertaining to regulated assets are allowed by the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (CERC) for recovery from beneficiaries. Exchange gains/losses arising after the date of commercial operation are also recoverable from beneficiaries as part of the rate-regulated asset mechanism.
  With effect from April 1, 2016, exchange gains/losses on long-term foreign currency monetary items relating to regulated assets are recoverable from beneficiaries as part of the rate-regulated asset mechanism. Accordingly, the Group is not exposed to significant foreign currency risk in respect of long-term foreign currency monetary items relating to regulated assets. Foreign exchange risk relating to long-term foreign currency exposures pertaining to non-regulated assets is managed through hedging strategies in accordance with the Group’s Foreign Exchange Risk Management Policy (FERMP). The exposure relating to short-term foreign currency monetary items is considered to be insignificant.
  The Group adopts a policy of hedging a portion of its estimated foreign currency exposure in respect of forecast transactions over the loan tenure. The Group uses a call spread option strategy consisting of purchased and written foreign currency call options to hedge its currency risk. These contracts are generally designated as cash flow hedges.
  The Group designates the intrinsic value of the call spread option strategy as the hedging instrument and applies a hedge ratio of 1:1. Changes in the time value of the call spread option strategy are excluded from the designation of the hedging instrument and are separately accounted for as cost of hedging, which is recognised in other equity under the Cost of Hedging Reserve. The Group’s policy is for the critical terms of the call spread option strategy to align with those of the hedged item.
  The Group determines the existence of an economic relationship between the hedging instrument and the hedged item based on the currency, amount and timing of their respective cash flows. The Group assesses whether the derivative designated in each hedging relationship is expected to be, and has been, effective in offsetting changes in the cash flows of the hedged item using the hypothetical derivative method.
  In these hedge relationships, the main sources of ineffectiveness are:
• the effect of the counterparty’s and the Group’s own credit risk on the fair value of the call spread option strategy, which is not 
reflected in the change in the fair value of the hedged cash flows attributable to changes in exchange rates; and
• changes in the timing of the hedged transactions.

 Master netting or similar agreements
  The Group enters into derivative transactions under International Swaps and Derivatives Association (ISDA) master netting 
agreements. In general, under these agreements the amounts owed by each counterparty on a single day in respect of all transactions outstanding in the same currency are aggregated into a single net amount that is payable by one party to the other. In certain circumstances, e.g. when a credit event such as a default occurs, all outstanding transactions under the agreement are terminated, the termination value is assessed and only a single net amount is payable in settlement of all transactions.

 Equity price risk
  Equity price risk is related to the change in market reference price of the investments in quoted equity securities. In the case of the Group, none of the investments in equity shares are quoted in the market and does not expose the Group to equity price risks.
Note 52 Disclosure as per Ind AS 115 'Revenue from Contract with the Customers'
1 Nature of Goods and Services
  The revenue of the Group comprises of income from energy sales, Coal sales, consultancy and other services. The following is a description of the principal activities:
A Revenue from energy sales
  The major revenue of the Group comes from energy sales. The Group sells electricity to customers mainly electricity utilities owned by State Governments. Sale of electricity is generally made pursuant to long-term Power Purchase Agreements (PPAs) entered into with the beneficiaries.
Product/Service Nature, timing of satisfaction of performance obligations and significant payment terms
Energy sales The Group recognises revenue from contracts for energy sales over time as the customers simultaneously 
receive and consume the benefits provided by the Group. The tariff for computing revenue from energy sales is determined in terms of CERC Regulations as notified from time to time. The amounts are billed on a 
monthly basis and are payable within contractually agreed credit period.
B Revenue from Coal sales
Product/Service Nature, timing of satisfaction of performance obligations and significant payment terms
Coal Sales In the case of sales through open market sales has been reckoned to the extent of amount received/as per sale terms when performance obligation is satisfied.
C Revenue from Lignite sales
  The Group supplies lignite from its captive mines to one of the power generating Group based on the fuel supply agreement entered 
with them. After meeting the internal demand, the remaining lignite are sold in the open market.
Product/Service Nature, timing of satisfaction of performance obligations and significant payment terms
Lignite Sales The Group recognises revenue from contracts for sale of captive lignite when control of the goods is 
transferred to customers. The amounts are billed as and when goods are transferred and are payable in accordance with the agreement entered with the party.
In the case of sales through open market sales has been reckoned to the extent of amount received/as per sale 
terms when performance obligation is satisfied.D Revenue from sales of fly ash and other by products
  The Group recognises revenue from sale of fly ash and other by-products upon transfer of control to the customer, generally upon 
dispatch, in accordance with the applicable terms of sale. Amounts are billed and collected as per the agreed contractual terms.

V. Transaction price allocated to the remaining performance obligations
  Revenue from sale of energy is accounted for based on tariff rates approved by the CERC (except items indicated as provisional) 
as modified by the orders of Appellate Tribunal for Electricity to the extent applicable. In case of power stations, where the tariff  rates are yet to be approved/items indicated provisional by the CERC in their orders, provisional rates are adopted considering the applicable CERC Tariff Regulations. Revenue from sale of energy is recognised once the electricity has been delivered to the beneficiary and is measured through a regular review of usage meters. Beneficiaries are billed on a periodic and regular basis. Therefore, transaction price to be allocated to remaining performance obligations cannot be determined reliably for the entire duration of the contract.
VI.  The Group does not expect to have any contracts where the period between the transfer of the promised goods or services to the customer and payment by the customer exceeds one year. As a consequence, the Group has not adjusted any of the transaction prices for the time value of money. The impact of subsequent modifications are duly recognised in the Statement of profit and loss.

Note 57
a) Disclosure in respect of Supplier Finance Arrangements
The Group participates in Supplier Finance Arrangements (SFAs), primarily through Trade Receivables Discounting System (TReDS) 
platforms, to facilitate early payment to its suppliers and optimise working capital. Under these arrangements, a finance provider settles the supplier’s invoice upon acceptance, and the Company subsequently settles the amount with the finance provider on the contractual due date. In cases where a supplier accepts the bid for its invoices on the TReDS platform, such arrangements are treated as SFAs.For arrangements that do not extend the original credit terms, the liabilities remain classified as 'Trade Payables - Others', and cash outflows are presented as operating activities.
There were no specific arrangements where the Group had renegotiated extended payment terms, which require, the reclassification 
of these amounts to 'Short-Term Borrowings' (representing a non-cash addition to borrowings). Hence, presentation of cash flows as financing activities did not arise.
Liquidity Risk Management:  In the event these financing facilities are withdrawn by the finance providers, the Group payment 
obligations to its suppliers revert to the standard contractual due dates. The Company maintains sufficient cash and unutilised fund-
based bank limits to comfortably settle these liabilities, thereby mitigating any significant liquidity risk.

j) Borrowings secured against current assets
  The group has availed working capital facility of H 5000 crore ( H 4000 crore Fund based and H 1000 crore non fund based.) agreed 
with SBI and is secured by Hypothecation of entire current assets of the group i.e. raw Materials, Stock in progress, Consumable stores, Spares and charge on receivables. The outstanding Working Capital loan as on 31.03.2025 is NIL (PY: H NIL) in the form 
of T-bill linked WCL.
  NTPL (Subsidiary company) availed working capital loan and cash credit facility agreed with Bank of India with Fund based Limit of H 1300.00 crore and Non-Fund based Limit of H 200.00 crore is subject to the availability of drawing power. The loan bears an 
interest rate of 6.70% p.a. (on the basis of Repo Rate + Mark Up 2.85% - BSD 2.15%) on Working capital demand loan and 8.55% p.a. (on the basis of 1 month MCLR plus 0.20% fixed spread) on Cash Credit. The loan is secured by pari passu charge on book debts, operating cash flows, receivables, all other current assets, commissions, revenues of whatsoever nature and wherever arising present & future relating to the project.
  In addition to the above NTPL (Subsidiary Company) has also availed State Bank of India Working Capital loan with Fund based Limit of H 1000 Crore and Non-Fund based Limit of H 10 crore (sub-limit of Fund based Limit of H 1000 crore) is subject to the 
availability of drawing power. This loan was Secured by pari passu first charge over the entire current assets of the Group i.e., hypothecation of raw materials, stock in process, finished goods, consumable stores, spares and charge on the receivables. The outstanding Working Capital loan as on 31.03.2025 is in the form of T-bill linked WCL.
  NUPPL signed an agreement of H 1,000 Crore ( H 900 Crore Fund Based & H 100 Crore Non-Fund Based) with SBI, CAG Branch 
for its requirement of working capital. The agreed interest rate for Cash Credit limit is 9.05% (3 months SBI MCLR+0.5% Spread) and for WCDL interest rate at mutually agreed rate at the time of availment, which is at present 8.70% (1 Month SBI MCLR+0.5%).
  The working capital loan is secured by exclusive Hypothecation Charge over the entire current assets of the Company (both present and future). NLCIL has also issued a letter of comfort in favour of State Bank of India for the working capital loan.
  The Group has filed quarterly/monthly returns with the banks and financial institutions as per the terms of loans. These returns are in agreement with books of accounts of the Group. There are no material discrepancies in the returns filed by the Group during the FY 2025-26 or any of previous financial years.

Note 61 Recent Pronouncement
The Ministry of Corporate Affairs (“MCA”) notifies new standards or amendments to existing standards under the Companies (Indian 
Accounting Standards) Rules from time to time. MCA has notified amendments to Ind AS 1 – Presentation of Financial Statements (classification of liabilities as current or non current, including liabilities with covenants), Ind AS 12 – Income Taxes (International Tax Reform – Pillar Two Model Rules), Ind AS 21 – The Effects of Changes in Foreign Exchange Rates (Lack of Exchangeability), and Ind AS 7 – Statement of Cash Flows and Ind AS 107 – Financial Instruments: Disclosures (Supplier Finance Arrangements), effective from April 1, 2025.
The Company has reviewed these amendments and based on its evaluation, has determined that they do not have any impact on the 
Company’s financial statements. However, pursuant to the adoption of the amendments to Ind AS 7 and Ind AS 107, the Company has provided the required disclosures relating to liabilities under supplier finance arrangements in the notes to the financial statements.
New standards or amendments not yet adopted
Classification of Liabilities as Current or Non-current and Non-current Liabilities with Covenants – Amendments to Ind AS 1- The amendments clarify that lender waivers obtained after the reporting date cannot be considered for the purpose of classifying liabilities as current or non current and require retrospective application in accordance with Ind AS 8.
These amendments are effective for reporting periods beginning on or after 1
st April, 2026. The Company does not expect any material 
impact on its financial statements.
Note 62 Additional Disclosures
a)  The Group has a system of obtaining periodic confirmation of balances from banks and other parties. There are no unconfirmed balances 
in respect of bank accounts and borrowings from banks & financial institutions. With regard to receivables for sale of energy, the Company sends demand intimations to the beneficiaries with details of amount paid and balance outstanding which can be said to be automatically confirmed on receipt of subsequent payment from such beneficiaries. In addition, reconciliation with beneficiaries for sale of power and lignite is generally done on periodical basis. So far as trade/other payables and loans and advances are concerned, the balance confirmation letters with the negative assertion as referred in the Standard on Auditing (SA) 505 (Revised) ‘External Confirmations’, were sent to the parties. Loan outstanding balances of employees are also reconciled periodically.b)  In the opinion of the management, the value of assets, other than property, plant and equipment and non-current investments, on realisation in the ordinary course of business, will not be less than the value at which these are stated in the Balance Sheet.
c)  The Company is facing with deficit in availability of land at Neyveli for lignite mining, which is impacting its operations. However, the Company is confident of overcoming the challenges on land acquisition at Neyveli mines with sustained efforts, in the near future. In order to ensure availability of lignite, the company has undertaken contingency mining with additional cost and resources.
d)  Due to Slow progress in Balance of Plant (BoP) package of Ghatampur Thermal Power Project, the Commissioning of the plant is delayed and may have corresponding impact on the project Cost. Government of India has approved the Revised cost estimate-II of H 21,780.94 
Cr on 12
th November 2024.Unit-1 COD has been declared on 12-12-2024. The tentative revised scheduled date of commissioning is 15-
07-2025 & 31-10-2025 for Unit-2 & Unit-3 respectively.
e)  As per the requirements of Rule 3(1) of the Companies (Accounts) Rules, 2014, the group has used SAP accounting software for maintaining its books of account, which has a feature of recording audit trail (edit log) facility that has operated throughout the year and has been preserved as per the statutory requirements for record retention. Further, the audit trail facility has also been enabled and preserved in respect of integrated external applications relating to Auction & Tender System, Integrated Weighment Tracking System, Employee Advance and Reimbursement Claims, GST Central Invoicing System, House Allotment, Rent Accounting and other township-related management systems.
f)  As per DIPAM guidelines, the minimum annual dividend payable is 30% of Profit After Tax (PAT) or 4% of Net Worth, whichever is higher, which amounted to H 770.81 crore for FY 2025-26.
  Considering the significant capital expenditure commitments and expansion plans of the Company, NLCIL sought exemption from payment of the minimum dividend requirement for FY 2024-25 and FY 2025-26. The Committee for Monitoring of Capital Management and Dividend in CPSEs (CMCDC), in its meeting held on 06 January 2026, granted exemption for FY 2024-25 and advised the Company to target a dividend payout of H 500 crore for FY 2025-26.
  Accordingly, the Company paid an interim dividend of H 499.19 crore (36%) on 10 February 2026 and has proposed a final dividend 
of H 34.67 crore (2.5%), resulting in a total dividend payout of H 533.86 crore (38.5%), in line with the target indicated by CMCDC for 
FY 2025-26. The total dividend payout represents 21.14% of PAT and 2.77% of Net Worth.
g)  NTPL has paid the dividend for the FY 2024-25, which is less than the minimum dividend criteria prescribed under the guidelines issued by DIPAM. NTPL has sought exemption from payment of Minimum Dividend and in line with the directions of MoC, the exemption was granted to NTPL from payment of Minimum Dividend.
  For FY 2025-26, Board of Directors of NTPL in their 150
th Meeting held on 11th May, 2026 has approved the proposal for seeking 
exemption from payment of minimum dividend. The approval of granting exemption to NTPL is under process.
h)  Subsequent to the balance sheet date, the Company identified certain events that provide additional evidence of conditions existing at the reporting date. Accordingly, necessary adjustments have been made in the financial statements. Management confirms that all material subsequent events up to the date of approval have been considered.
i)  The consolidated financial statements for the year ended March 31, 2026, were approved for issue by the Board of Directors of the company on May 13, 2026.
j)  The Group has assessed the impact of the Code on Wages, 2019 and related labour codes, and does not expect any material impact on the financial statements.
k)  The Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (DPDP Act) encompasses the entire organisational ecosystem and has implications across all functions, business units, and support processes. Accordingly, it is being addressed as a strategic, enterprise-wide priority with active oversight at the highest levels of the Organisation.
  The activities related to the DPDP Act are currently under active deliberation by the relevant internal stakeholders. The Management is cognisant of the regulatory framework and the compliance requirements thereunder.
  The requisite steps, including those pertaining to consent management, awareness training, policy review, and control framework assessment, etc., shall be undertaken in a structured and time-bound manner as per the extant MeitY guidelines.
l)  The Company has performed a detailed assessment of the recognition criteria prescribed under Paragraph 9 of Appendix B to Ind AS 16. Based on this assessment, the Company has concluded that for its over burden removal mining operations, the required conditions specified under Paragraph 9 of Appendix B to Ind AS 16 relating to recognition of stripping asset were not met. Accordingly, the related transactions have been accounted for appropriately in accordance with the applicable Indian Accounting Standards. 
 Inline with industry practice, the policy in this regard shall be reviewed at end of each financial year.
